Using simultaneous five -wavelength illumination spanning 500–700 nm, we experimentally demonstrate the parallel approximation of 4,136 nonlinear functions.
CLM-PHOT-0079.statement: Under five-wavelength illumination spanning 500–700 nm, a single-layer diffractive processor experimentally achieved parallel approximation of 4,136 distinct nonlinear functions.

Figure 8a shows the optical layout and experimental setup, in which a phase -only SLM implements the co -localized encoder and decoder (E+D), and a camera records the output intensities over spatially separated detector regions.
Approximation accuracy can therefore remain limited when target nonlinear functions require frequency components that are inadequately represented by the available computational Fourier features.

In practical implementations, factors such as encoder dispersion, finite phase -modulation range, optical throughput, detector response and experimental noise can further influence the achievable accuracy.
